records.source: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־נֹ֖חַ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And blessed God Noah and his sons and said to them, be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
pieces: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.

L.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

R.1: Then God blessed Noah and his sons. He said to them, "Have many children, so that there are more and more of you, and fill the earth.

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth: the blessing of 1:28 renewed
decisions.reason: God gives Noah and his sons the blessing he gave the first human beings (1:28), word for word. Humankind begins again, with the same calling. The command to "subdue" the earth is not repeated.

records.heading: God blesses Noah and his sons

records.source: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כָּל־חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] fear of you and [the] dread of you will be on every animal of the earth and on every bird of the heavens, on all that creeps [on] the ground and on all [the] fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.
pieces: Every animal on the earth, every bird of the sky, every creature that moves along the ground and all the fish of the sea will fear you and dread you. They are placed in your power.

L.2: And the fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth and on every bird of the heavens, on everything that creeps on the ground and on all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.

R.2: All the animals, birds, small creatures and fish will be afraid of you. I am putting them under your control.

decisions.choice: fear and dread of you: the relation between people and animals changes
decisions.reason: Humankind still rules the animals (1:26-28), but the relationship is no longer peaceful: animals will fear people, who will now kill them for food (verse 3). Isaiah looks forward to a time when this fear ends (Isaiah 11:6-9).

decisions.choice: into your hand they are given: placed in your power
decisions.reason: "Into your hand" means into your control, a phrase used of victory over enemies (Deuteronomy 20:13).

records.source: כָּל־רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָ֑ה כְּיֶ֣רֶק עֵ֔שֶׂב נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־כֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: Every moving thing that is alive will be food for you; like [the] green plants I give you everything.
pieces: Every living thing that moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.

L.3: Every moving thing that is alive will be food for you; as [I gave] the green plants, I give you everything.

R.3: You may eat any animal that lives and moves. I gave you green plants to eat, and now I give you everything.

decisions.choice: as the green plants, I give you everything: 1:29-30 widened
decisions.reason: In 1:29-30 God gave plants for food. Now he gives animals as well, with one limit (verse 4). The verb "I give" repeats 1:29.

decisions.choice: as [I gave] the green plants
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "like the green plants"; Literal brackets the words that make the comparison clear.

records.source: אַךְ־בָּשָׂ֕ר בְּנַפְשׁ֥וֹ דָמ֖וֹ לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.
pieces: But you must not eat meat that still has its lifeblood in it.

L.4: But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.

R.4: But you must not eat meat that still has blood in it, because the blood is its life.

decisions.choice: flesh with its life, its blood: life belongs to God
decisions.reason: The blood is treated as the life of the creature, and life belongs to God who gives it. So blood is not to be eaten; it is poured out (Leviticus 17:10-14; Deuteronomy 12:23-24). The rule applies to all humankind, not only to Israel, and the early church kept it (Acts 15:20, 29).

decisions.choice: life: the word often translated soul
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the life of a living creature, as in 1:20 and 2:7.

decisions.choice: its lifeblood
decisions.reason: Balanced joins "its life, its blood" into one word that says both.

records.source: וְאַ֨ךְ אֶת־דִּמְכֶ֤ם לְנַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ אֶדְרֹ֔שׁ מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־חַיָּ֖ה אֶדְרְשֶׁ֑נּוּ וּמִיַּ֣ד הָֽאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ הָֽאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And surely your blood, for your lives, I will require; from [the] hand of every animal I will require it, and from [the] hand of humankind, from [the] hand of each man his brother I will require the life of humankind.
pieces: And for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting. I will demand it from every animal, and from every human being: from each person I will demand an accounting for the life of another.

L.5: And surely for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning; from every animal I will require it, and from {{gender:humankind|man}}; from each one, for the life of {{gender:another|his brother}}, I will require the life of {{gender:a human being|man}}.

R.5: If anyone takes a human life, I will hold them to account. If an animal kills a person, I will hold it to account. And if one person kills another, I will hold the killer to account.

decisions.choice: require: demand an accounting for
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or to demand back. God will call to account whoever, animal or human, takes a human life (Exodus 21:28; Psalm 9:13).

decisions.choice: each one, his brother: every person, for another person
decisions.reason: "Each man ... his brother" is a Hebrew way of saying "one another". Every human being is the other's brother; murder is always the killing of a brother, as with Cain (4:8-11).

decisions.choice: each one ... another ... a human being; with the traditional setting, his brother, man
decisions.reason: The words mean every person, man or woman; the default is inclusive.

records.source: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הָֽאָדָ֔ם בָּֽאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ כִּ֚י בְּצֶ֣לֶם אֱלֹהִ֔ים עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The one] shedding [the] blood of humankind, by humankind his blood will be shed; for in [the] image of God he made humankind.
pieces: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human being that person's blood will be shed; for God made human beings in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own image.

L.6: Whoever sheds the blood of {{gender:a human being|man}}, by {{gender:a human being|man}} {{gender:that person's|his}} blood will be shed; for in the image of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{gender:humankind|man}}.

R.6: Whoever kills a person must be put to death by others, because God made people to be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: whoever sheds ... by a human being his blood will be shed: a poem of exact justice
alternatives: in exchange for the human, his blood will be shed
decisions.reason: The first line is poetry, its words in mirror order (sheds, blood, human / human, blood, shed). "By a human being" most likely means that the penalty is carried out by human hands, so that God gives humankind the duty of justice for murder. The small word can also mean "in exchange for": a life for a life.

decisions.choice: for in the image of God he made humankind: the reason human life is sacred
decisions.reason: Murder is an attack on God's own image (1:26-27). Even after the flood, and after all the evil of 6:5, every human being still bears the image of God.

decisions.choice: he made (Literal), his own image (Balanced), like him (Readable): deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֖ם פְּר֣וּ וּרְב֑וּ שִׁרְצ֥וּ בָאָ֖רֶץ וּרְבוּ־בָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: And you, be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply on it.
pieces: As for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread over the earth and multiply on it."

L.7: And you, be fruitful and multiply, swarm on the earth and multiply on it."

R.7: As for you, have many children. Spread out over the earth and fill it."

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply: the blessing repeated
decisions.reason: The speech ends as it began (verse 1): life, not death, is God's purpose. "Swarm" is the word used of the creatures in 1:20-21 and 8:17.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־נֹ֔חַ וְאֶל־בָּנָ֥יו אִתּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said God to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
pieces: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,

L.8: And God said to Noah and to his sons with him,

R.8: Then God said to Noah and his sons,

records.heading: The covenant and the bow in the clouds

records.source: וַאֲנִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י מֵקִ֛ים אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם אַֽחֲרֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I, here I [am] establishing my covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
pieces: "I now establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you and with your descendants after you,

L.9: "And I, look, I am establishing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you and with your offspring after you,

R.9: "I am making a covenant with you and with your children and their children after you,

decisions.choice: my covenant: the covenant promised in 6:18
decisions.reason: God now sets up the covenant he promised Noah before the flood. It is God's own covenant: he makes it and binds himself by it, and asks nothing in return.

decisions.choice: your offspring after you: all future generations
decisions.reason: The covenant includes all of Noah's descendants, that is, all humankind.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־נֶ֤פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֔ם בָּע֧וֹף בַּבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ אִתְּכֶ֑ם מִכֹּל֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י הַתֵּבָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and with every living creature that [is] with you, among the birds, among the livestock, and among every animal of the earth with you, of all that came out of the ark, to every animal of the earth.
pieces: and with every living creature that was with you, the birds, the livestock and all the wild animals, all those that came out of the ark with you, every living creature on earth.

L.10: and with every living creature that [is] with you, the birds, the livestock and every animal of the earth with you, of all that came out of the ark, every animal of the earth.

R.10: and with every living thing that was with you on the boat: the birds, the farm animals and the wild animals. This covenant is with every living thing on earth.

decisions.choice: every living creature: the covenant includes the animals
decisions.reason: The covenant is made with the animals too: God's promise covers all life on earth (Hosea 2:18).

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת כָּל־בָּשָׂ֛ר ע֖וֹד מִמֵּ֣י הַמַּבּ֑וּל וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד מַבּ֖וּל לְשַׁחֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will establish my covenant with you, and not will be cut off all flesh again by [the] waters of the flood, and not will there be again a flood to destroy the earth.
pieces: I establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you: never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."

L.11: And I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you: never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."

R.11: This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise: I will never again destroy all life with a flood. There will never again be a flood that destroys the earth."

decisions.choice: be cut off: be destroyed
decisions.reason: "Cut off" means destroyed or wiped out. It is also the verb used for making a covenant ("cutting" a covenant, 15:18); the promise is that life will not be cut off.

decisions.choice: never again a flood to destroy the earth: God's unconditional promise
decisions.reason: God binds himself, without conditions, never to destroy all life by a flood again (8:21). The promise does not depend on human goodness.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֗ן בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֑ם לְדֹרֹ֖ת עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said God, this [is the] sign of the covenant that I [am] making between me and you and every living creature that [is] with you, for generations forever:
pieces: And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:

L.12: And God said, "This [is] the sign of the covenant that I am making between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and every living creature that [is] with you, for all generations to come:

R.12: And God said, "Here is the sign of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to you and to every living thing with you, for all time to come:

decisions.choice: sign of the covenant: a visible token of the promise
decisions.reason: A sign is something that can be seen and that points to something else. Each of God's covenants in Genesis and Exodus has one: the bow here, circumcision with Abraham (17:11), the Sabbath at Sinai (Exodus 31:13).

decisions.choice: for generations forever: for all time
decisions.reason: "For everlasting generations" means without end.

records.source: אֶת־קַשְׁתִּ֕י נָתַ֖תִּי בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: My bow I have set in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
pieces: I have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the earth.

L.13: I have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of the covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and the earth.

R.13: I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to the earth.

decisions.choice: my bow: the rainbow, called by the word for a warrior's bow
alternatives: only the rainbow, with no further sense
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a bow used in war or hunting. God calls the rainbow "my bow". Many readers see in it a picture of God setting aside his weapon of judgment, hanging up his bow; the text itself says only that it is the sign of the covenant.

decisions.choice: I have set: a gift made as God speaks
alternatives: I set (in the past, at creation)
decisions.reason: The completed verb form is used, as in 1:29, for an act done by the words that announce it: God now appoints the bow as the sign.

decisions.choice: rainbow
decisions.reason: Readable says "rainbow", which is what the bow is, so that young readers do not picture a weapon; the sense of the warrior's bow is explained in m1.

records.source: וְהָיָ֕ה בְּעַֽנְנִ֥י עָנָ֖ן עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנִרְאֲתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּעָנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when I bring clouds over the earth, and is seen the bow in the cloud,
pieces: Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the clouds,

L.14: And it will be, when I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the cloud,

R.14: Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears,

records.source: וְזָכַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה ע֤וֹד הַמַּ֨יִם֙ לְמַבּ֔וּל לְשַׁחֵ֖ת כָּל־בָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: and I will remember my covenant which [is] between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and not will again the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.
pieces: I will remember {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.

L.15: then I will remember {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant that [is] between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.

R.15: I will remember {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to you and to every living thing. The water will never again become a flood that destroys all life.

decisions.choice: I will remember: I will act on my promise
decisions.reason: As in 8:1, God's remembering means acting faithfully on his commitment, not recalling something he had forgotten. The sign is for God as well as for people: when he sees it, he keeps his word.

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וּרְאִיתִ֗יהָ לִזְכֹּר֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֔ים וּבֵין֙ כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה בְּכָל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And will be the bow in the cloud, and I will see it to remember [the] everlasting covenant between God and every living creature among all flesh that [is] on the earth.
pieces: When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind on the earth."

L.16: And the bow will be in the cloud, and I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that [is] on the earth."

R.16: When I see the rainbow in the clouds, I will remember the promise that will last forever between God and every living thing on earth."

decisions.choice: everlasting covenant: a covenant without end
decisions.reason: The phrase is used later of God's covenants with Abraham (17:7) and David (2 Samuel 23:5). Isaiah 54:9-10 recalls this covenant as a picture of God's lasting love.

decisions.choice: between God and every living creature: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself as "God", as rulers and judges sometimes did, which makes the promise sound like a solemn legal statement.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־נֹ֑חַ זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲקִמֹ֔תִי בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֥ין כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ
records.gloss: And said God to Noah, this [is the] sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that [is] on the earth.
pieces: So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I have established between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and all life on the earth."

L.17: And God said to Noah, "This [is] the sign of the covenant that I have established between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and all flesh that [is] on the earth."

R.17: So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the promise I have made with every living thing on earth."

records.source: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ בְנֵי־נֹ֗חַ הַיֹּֽצְאִים֙ מִן־הַתֵּבָ֔ה שֵׁ֖ם וְחָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וְחָ֕ם ה֖וּא אֲבִ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And were [the] sons of Noah who came out from the ark Shem and Ham and Japheth; and Ham, he [was the] father of Canaan.
pieces: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

L.18: And the sons of Noah who came out from the ark were Shem and Ham and Japheth; and Ham was the father of Canaan.

R.18: Noah's sons who came out of the boat were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

decisions.choice: Ham was the father of Canaan: preparing for verses 22-27
decisions.reason: The note prepares for the story that follows, where Canaan, Ham's son, is cursed. Canaan is the ancestor of the peoples of the land of Canaan (10:15-19), whom Israel later met there.

records.heading: Noah's sons

records.source: שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה נָֽפְצָ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Three these [were the] sons of Noah, and from these was spread all the earth.
pieces: These three were the sons of Noah, and from them came all the people who spread over the earth.

L.19: These three [were] the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was populated.

R.19: These three were Noah's sons. All the people on earth came from them.

decisions.choice: from these the whole earth spread out: all peoples descend from them
decisions.reason: "The whole earth" means all the people of the earth (as in 11:1). Chapter 10 lists the peoples who came from the three sons.

records.source: וַיָּ֥חֶל נֹ֖חַ אִ֣ישׁ הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וַיִּטַּ֖ע כָּֽרֶם׃
records.gloss: And began Noah, the man of the ground, and he planted a vineyard.
pieces: Noah, a man of the soil, was the first to plant a vineyard.

L.20: And Noah, a man of the ground, began [farming] and planted a vineyard.

R.20: Noah was a farmer. He was the first person to plant a vineyard.

decisions.choice: Noah, a man of the soil, began: he was the first to plant a vineyard
alternatives: Noah began to be a farmer
decisions.reason: The verb "began" can go with "man of the soil" (he began to farm) or with "planted" (he was the first to plant a vineyard). The second fits the stories of first things in these chapters (4:20-22, 26). "Man of the soil" recalls Lamech's hope for relief from the ground (5:29).

decisions.choice: began [farming]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets an object for "began", which has none in the Hebrew.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מִן־הַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁכָּ֑ר וַיִּתְגַּ֖ל בְּת֥וֹךְ אָהֳלֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And he drank some of the wine and became drunk, and uncovered himself in [the] middle of his tent.
pieces: When he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered inside his tent.

L.21: And he drank some of the wine and became drunk, and he lay uncovered inside his tent.

R.21: He drank some of the wine he made and got drunk. Then he lay naked in his tent.

decisions.choice: became drunk: the righteous man's failure
decisions.reason: Noah, called righteous and blameless (6:9), fails after the flood. The text reports it without excuse. Scripture elsewhere warns against drunkenness and the shame it brings (Proverbs 20:1; 23:29-35; Habakkuk 2:15).

decisions.choice: uncovered himself: lay exposed
decisions.reason: The verb means to uncover or expose oneself; in his drunkenness Noah lies naked.

records.source: וַיַּ֗רְא חָ֚ם אֲבִ֣י כְנַ֔עַן אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יו וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לִשְׁנֵֽי־אֶחָ֖יו בַּחֽוּץ׃
records.gloss: And saw Ham, [the] father of Canaan, the nakedness of his father, and told [it] to his two brothers outside.
pieces: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father naked and went out and told his two brothers.

L.22: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

R.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father lying naked. He went outside and told his two brothers about it.

decisions.choice: saw his father's nakedness: looked on his father's shame
alternatives: a sexual act against Noah (or Noah's wife)
decisions.reason: "To see the nakedness" of someone can be a way of speaking of sexual relations (Leviticus 20:17), and some take it so here. But the next verse answers it exactly with covering and not seeing, which suggests that the wrong was Ham's looking on and telling, disgracing his father instead of covering his shame.

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ שֵׁ֨ם וָיֶ֜פֶת אֶת־הַשִּׂמְלָ֗ה וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ֙ עַל־שְׁכֶ֣ם שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וַיְכַסּ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶם֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וְעֶרְוַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And took Shem and Japheth the garment and put [it] on [the] shoulder of both of them and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father, and their faces [were] backward, and the nakedness of their father they did not see.
pieces: But Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders and walked in backward to cover their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away, so they did not see their father naked.

L.23: And Shem and Japheth took the garment and laid it on both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered their father's nakedness; their faces [were turned] backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.

R.23: But Shem and Japheth took a cloak and held it over their shoulders. They walked backward into the tent and covered their father. They kept their faces turned away so that they would not see him naked.

decisions.choice: covered ... did not see: honoring their father
decisions.reason: The brothers do the opposite of Ham: they cover what he looked on, and they do not see. Covering another's shame is a mark of love (Proverbs 10:12; 1 Peter 4:8). They honor their father as the later commandment requires (Exodus 20:12).

records.source: וַיִּ֥יקֶץ נֹ֖חַ מִיֵּינ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה־ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃
records.gloss: And awoke Noah from his wine and knew what had done to him his son the youngest.
pieces: When Noah awoke from his wine and found out what his youngest son had done to him,

L.24: And Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him.

R.24: When Noah woke up and was sober again, he found out what his youngest son had done to him.

decisions.choice: his youngest son: Ham, the youngest
decisions.reason: The word means small or young; with the article it usually means the youngest. Ham is listed second (5:32; 9:18), so the list is not in order of birth. Some take "son" to mean grandson, Canaan, who is cursed next.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָר֣וּר כְּנָ֑עַן עֶ֥בֶד עֲבָדִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְאֶחָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he said, cursed [be] Canaan; a slave of slaves he will be to his brothers.
pieces: he said, "Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest of servants to his brothers."

L.25: And he said, "Cursed [be] Canaan; a slave of slaves he will be to his brothers."

R.25: He said, "May there be a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest servant of his brothers."

decisions.choice: cursed be Canaan: Noah curses Ham's son, not Ham
decisions.reason: Noah's words are a prophetic curse on Canaan, Ham's son. The text does not explain why Canaan rather than Ham is named; it looks ahead to the Canaanites, whose land Israel later took and whose practices the law condemns (Leviticus 18:3, 24-28). The words are Noah's, not God's.

decisions.choice: the misuse of this verse: it names Canaan, not any race
decisions.reason: In modern times this verse was wrongly used to justify the enslavement of Africans, under the false idea of a "curse of Ham". The text curses Canaan only. It says nothing about skin color or race, and Canaan's descendants lived in the land of Canaan (10:15-19), not in Africa.

decisions.choice: a slave of slaves: the lowest of slaves
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun this way expresses the extreme ("song of songs", "holy of holies"). The word is the ordinary word for a slave.

decisions.choice: the lowest of servants
decisions.reason: "The lowest of servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "a slave of slaves", and the meaning decision (m3) keeps the sense. The curse is that Canaan will be subject to his brothers, as Esau's line is to Jacob's in 27:37, where the word is also rendered with "serve".

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּר֥וּךְ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹ֣הֵי שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said, blessed [be] YHWH, [the] God of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to them.
pieces: He also said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Shem! May Canaan be his servant.

L.26: And he said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be his slave.

R.26: He also said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Shem! May Canaan be Shem's servant.

decisions.choice: blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem: Shem's blessing is his God
decisions.reason: Instead of blessing Shem directly, Noah blesses the LORD as Shem's God. The line of Shem leads to Abraham (11:10-26) and to Israel, the people who will know God by this name.

decisions.choice: his slave: the slave of Shem (or of Shem's people)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun can be singular or plural ("to him" or "to them"); it refers to Shem, or to Shem and his descendants.

decisions.choice: Shem's servant
decisions.reason: Readable names Shem so that "his" is not taken to mean God's (m2).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: יַ֤פְתְּ אֱלֹהִים֙ לְיֶ֔פֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּ֖ן בְּאָֽהֳלֵי־שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: May God make spacious for Japheth, and let him dwell in [the] tents of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to them.
pieces: May God make room for Japheth, and may he live in the tents of Shem. May Canaan be his servant."

L.27: May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be his slave."

R.27: May God give Japheth lots of room to spread out. May Japheth live peacefully with Shem's people, and may Canaan be his servant."

decisions.choice: enlarge Japheth: a play on his name
decisions.reason: "May he enlarge" (yaft) sounds like the name Japheth (Yefet). Noah prays that Japheth's descendants will have room to spread, as the many peoples of 10:2-5 do.

decisions.choice: let him dwell in the tents of Shem: Japheth sharing in Shem's blessing
alternatives: let God dwell in the tents of Shem
decisions.reason: "He" most likely means Japheth: he will live peacefully with Shem and share in his blessing. Some read "he" as God, who will dwell among Shem's people. The verse does not decide.

decisions.choice: May Japheth live peacefully with Shem's people
alternatives: let him dwell in the tents of Shem
decisions.reason: Readable takes "he" as Japheth (m2) and explains the picture of sharing tents.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַֽיְחִי־נֹ֖חַ אַחַ֣ר הַמַּבּ֑וּל שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַֽחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And lived Noah after the flood three hundred year[s] and fifty year[s].
pieces: After the flood Noah lived 350 years.

L.28: And Noah lived after the flood 350 years.

R.28: Noah lived 350 years after the flood.

records.source: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כָּל־יְמֵי־נֹ֔חַ תְּשַׁ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃פ
records.gloss: And were all [the] days of Noah nine hundred year[s] and fifty year[s], and he died.
pieces: Altogether, Noah lived 950 years, and then he died.

L.29: And all the days of Noah were 950 years, and he died.

R.29: Noah lived to be 950 years old, and then he died.

decisions.choice: and he died: the refrain of chapter 5
decisions.reason: Noah's life closes with the words used for each father in chapter 5. His genealogy, begun in 5:32, is now complete.
